Python is 3.10+ (help section header is `options:`, not `optional arguments:`). ## 1. Exit codes | Case | RC | |---|---| | all three options supplied (any order) | `0` | | `--help` / `-h` (anywhere, even with other/bad args) | `0` | | any parse error (missing required, unrecognized, missing value, explicit-arg-to-flag) | `2` | ## 2. Streams - Success output (4 `print()`s) → **stdout**, nothing on stderr. - Help text → **stdout** only (stderr empty; verified `--help 2>&1 1>/dev/null` produced 0 bytes). - All error output (usage line + error line) → **stderr** only; **stdout is byte-empty** on error (verified with `od -c`: 0 bytes). ## 3. Program name `os.path.basename(argv[0])`. Verified: symlink `/tmp/foo` → `usage: foo …`; `exec -a weirdname` → `usage: weirdname …`; copy `/tmp/bar` → `usage: bar …`. Under normal invocation it is exactly `test13_executable`. JS: use `path.basename(process.argv[1])`. ## 4. Usage line (used by both help and errors) ``` usage: test13_executable [-h] --a A --b B --c C ``` Exactly one `\n` terminator, no trailing spaces (`cat -A` shows `…--c C$`). ## 5. Option syntax - `--a VALUE` and `--a=VALUE` both work; `--a=x=y` → value `x=y` (split on first `=` only). `--a=` → empty string value. - Repeats: **last wins** (`store` action). `--a first --a second` → `second`. `--c C1 --c C2` → `C2`. - Order-independent: `--c C --b B --a A` works identically. - Single-dash `-a` is **not** an alias for `--a` (treated as an unknown option → see precedence above). - Case-sensitive: `--A` is not `--a`. - Prefix abbreviation is **enabled** (`allow_abbrev` default True) but only `--help` is abbreviable here: `--h`, `--he`, `--hel` all print help, RC 0. `--a/--b/--c` are already minimal; no ambiguous-prefix error is reachable with this option set. - `fromfile_prefix_chars` is NOT set: `@file` is an ordinary (unrecognized) token. ## 7. ## 12. Implementation notes for the JS port

1. Model the block-HTML extractor as a tag-balance scanner over a proper HTML tokenizer, not a blank-line-delimited CommonMark HTML block.
2. Recognition requires a block-level tag at column 0 (case-insensitive name lookup against the §1 list). Otherwise the line is markdown and any HTML on it is inline-raw.
3. Once a block is extracted from a line, continue scanning the same line's remainder for further block-level HTML (producing extra split lines and, for void elements/comments, relocation after the following paragraph). If the line did not start with a block tag, do not extract at all.
4. Unbalanced open tag → consume verbatim to EOF (including blank lines). Incomplete closing tag (``) → emit what was consumed and **drop the rest**. Unclosed comment → not a block, escape `<`. Unclosed PI → append `\n\n?>`.
5. Separator rule: join top-level items with `\n`, but emit `\n\n` after a raw block-HTML item that was followed by a blank line and by further content; strip leading/trailing blank lines; collapse runs of blank lines to one.
6. `--a` pipeline must include md_in_html (`markdown="1"|"block"|"span"`): strip the `markdown` attribute, process the interior as markdown/inline, and re-serialize the wrapper element with normalized attributes (`name="value"` double-quoted, booleans as `name="name"`, source order preserved) and children at column 0. `--b`, `--c`, and the combined pass must NOT.

--c '# H {: #custom }'  -> 
            H {: #custom }
            
```
Contrast (single run, `--a`/`--b`/`--c` all `'# H {: #custom }'`):
```

            H
                            <-- html1: extra ⊃ attr_list, no toc, id from attr_list

            H {: #custom }
                           <-- html2: codehilite, no id

            H {: #custom }
             <-- html3: toc slug
```

**SURPRISE — pre-existing ids from raw HTML are not reserved, so duplicate `id`s are emitted:**
```
IN  --c $'
            x
            \n\n# real'
OUT 
            x
            
    
    
            real
            
```
(note the literal blank line after the raw-HTML block). The `used_ids` set is seeded only from tree elements carrying `id`, and in `--c` nothing can produce one, so it is effectively always empty at start.

## 7. fenced_code interaction

`#` inside a fence never becomes a heading and gets no id; `[TOC]` inside a fence is left literal.
```
--c $'```\n# not a heading\n[TOC]\n```\n\n# real'
  -> 
            # not a heading
     [TOC]
     
            
     
            real
            
--c $'~~~\n# in tilde fence\n~~~\n\n# real'
  -> 
            # in tilde fence
     
            
     
            real
            
--c $'    # indented code\n\n# real'
  -> 
            # indented code
     
            
     
            real
            
--c $'```python\n# comment\n```\n\n[TOC]\n\n# real'
  -> 
            # comment
     
            
     
            
     ...
```

## 8. Cross-check: no ids in `--a` / `--b`

```
--a $'# Hello World\n## Two\n\n[TOC]'  and  --b same
html1: 
            Hello World
            \n
            Two
            \n
            [TOC]
            
html2: 
            Hello World
            \n
            Two
            \n
            [TOC]
            
```
Neither `extra`+`tables` nor `codehilite` adds heading ids, and `[TOC]` is inert in both (stays a literal paragraph).
